title: Responding to objections to recursive self-improvement
description:
I responded to the strongest objections that people had about the RSI essay.

Watch on YouTube; read the transcript.

Timestamps

(00:00:00) – “Do you have a real job?”

(00:02:41) – Cindy Wu: Is AI research a verifiable domain?

(00:11:10) – corsaren: The overarching objection

(00:12:20) – corsaren: Are the essay’s examples sloppy intuition pumps?

(00:13:51) – corsaren: Is online learning AI’s Millennium Prize problem?

(00:17:39) – corsaren: Is human evolution evidence for transfer?

(00:22:20) – corsaren: Can scaling RL let AIs ramp quickly in new contexts?

(00:25:31) – Why take Paul Christiano’s predictions seriously?

(00:26:26) – Intuitions for what superintelligence could be like

(00:29:26) – Paul’s 2018 prediction and the Hugging Face incident

(00:32:44) – How would superhuman AIs actually take over?

(00:35:12) – What should we do about AI motivations?

(00:40:54) – Séb Krier: Won’t many different models constrain each other?

(00:44:09) – Henry Zhang: Is METR’s finding just one data point?

(00:49:13) – Agustin Lebron: Is it still recursive if humans are in the loop?

(00:53:07) – Peli: Does AI’s success in math transfer to AI research?

(00:56:20) – Henry Dowling: Will AI research be bottlenecked on compute?

(01:00:21) – Takeaways, and the next couple of years

(01:03:30) – Would we even know?

(01:03:57) – Closing thoughts



This is a public episode. If you would like to discuss this with other subscribers or get access to bonus episodes, visit www.dwarkesh.com
